paras.text: Consider ethene (C₂H₄) to illustrate the structure of alkenes. In ethene, each carbon atom has three sp²-hybridized orbitals which are coplanar. One of the sp²-hybrid orbitals of one carbon atom overlaps linearly with that of another carbon atom to form a sigma (δ) bond. The other two sp²-hybrid orbitals of each carbon atom overlap with 1s orbital of hydrogen atoms to form C-H sigma bonds. The unhybridized p-orbitals of the two carbon atoms, which remain perpendicular to the plane of hybridized orbitals, overlap in a side-wise (parallel) fashion to form a pi (π) bond between the two carbon atoms. (Figure.16.3).

paras.text: If an alkene has two double bonds, it is called a diene (or alkadiene), if three double bonds, then triene (or alkatriene) and so on. When two double bonds in an alkene (diene, triene etc) are separated by just one single bond, the two double bonds are said to be conjugated and the alkene is a conjugated alkene. The interaction between the two double bonds in a conjugated dienes (or triene etc.) delocalizes the electron density and increases the stability of the molecule, and termed as conjugation. The simplest diene that can have two conjugated pi bonds is buta-1,3-diene. Similarly hexa-1,3,5-triene is a triene with three conjugated double bonds and so on.

(b) IUPAC System

The IUPAC rules for naming alkenes are;

i. Select the longest continuous carbon chain that include the maximum number of double bonds.

ii. The name given to the longest chain will act as parent name, whereby the suffix -ane of the corresponding alkane is replaced by suffix -ene.

iii. If there are two double bonds, the suffix is -diene; for three, -triene; for four, -tetraene; and so on, are used.

iv. Number the chain from the end that gives lower number to the doubly bonded carbons.

v. Since double bond appears between two carbon atoms, therefore its position is indicated by the number of that carbon atom, bearing lower number and this number is written before suffix -ene, -diene etc.

vi. Carbon-carbon double bonds take precedence over alkyl groups in determining the main carbon chain and the direction in which it is numbered.

vii. Name substituent groups as in alkanes, indicating their locations by the number of the main-chain carbon to which they are attached.

viii. For compounds that show geometric isomerism, add the appropriate prefix: cis- or trans-.(see section 16.6)

The unhybridized p-orbitals of the two carbon atoms, which remain perpendicular to the plane of hybridized orbitals, overlap in a side-wise (parallel) fashion to form a pi (π) bond between the two carbon atoms. (Figure.16.3).

د الکینونو د جوړښت د روښانولو لپاره ایتین (C₂H₄) په پام کې ونیسئ. په ایتین کې هر کاربني اټوم درې sp² هایبرډ اوربیټلونه لري چې په یوه سطحه کې دي. د یوه کاربني اټوم یو sp² هایبرډ اوربیټل د بل کاربني اټوم له همداسې اوربیټل سره خطي پوښښ کوي، څو سیګما (δ) تړون جوړ کړي. د هر کاربني اټوم نور دوه sp² هایبرډ اوربیټلونه د هایدروجني اټومونو له 1s اوربیټلونو سره پوښښ کوي، څو C–H سیګما تړونونه جوړ کړي. د دواړو کاربني اټومونو غیر هایبرډ p اوربیټلونه، چې د هایبرډ اوربیټلونو سطحې ته عمودي پاتې کېږي، په اړخیز (موازي) ډول پوښښ کوي، څو د دواړو کاربني اټومونو ترمنځ پای (π) تړون جوړ کړي. (شکل16.3).

لنډ معلومات

په 1993 کې IUPAC په نومونو کې د کارېدونکو شمېرو په موقعیتونو کې د منطقي بدلون سپارښتنه وکړه. د بنسټیز نوم مخکې د شمېرو د لیکلو (1-butene) پر ځای یې سپارښتنه وکړه چې شمېرې سم د نوم له هغې برخې مخکې ولیکل شي چې موقعیت یې ښيي (but-1-ene).

شکل16.3 په ایتین کې د سیګما او پای تړونونو په جوړېدو کې د اوربیټلونو د پوښښ تشریح.

د ایتین ټولیز جوړښت هوار دی، چې د H–C–C او H–C–H تړوني زاویې پکې نږدې 120° دي. د کاربن–کاربن دوه ګوني تړون اوږدوالی 134 pm او د C–H تړونونو اوږدوالی 108 pm دی.

16.5.3 کنجوګېشن

که الکین دوه دوه ګوني تړونونه ولري، ډایین (یا الکاډایین) بلل کېږي؛ که درې ولري، ټرایین (یا الکاټرایین) او همداسې نور. کله چې په الکین (ډایین، ټرایین او نورو) کې دوه دوه ګوني تړونونه یوازې په یوه یو ګوني تړون سره جلا وي، دواړه دوه ګوني تړونونه کنجوګېټ شوي او الکین کنجوګېټ شوی الکین بلل کېږي. په کنجوګېټ شوي ډایین (یا ټرایین او نورو) کې د دوو دوه ګونو تړونونو ترمنځ متقابل اغېز د الکترون کثافت غیر موضعي کوي او د مالیکول ثبات زیاتوي، او کنجوګېشن بلل کېږي. تر ټولو ساده ډایین چې دوه کنجوګېټ شوي پای تړونونه لرلی شي، بیوټا-1،3-ډایین دی. همدارنګه هیکسا-1،3،5-ټرایین د دریو کنجوګېټ شوو دوه ګونو تړونونو لرونکی ټرایین دی، او همداسې نور.

Greek letters, α, β, γ etc. are used to distinguish isomers having double bonds at different positions.

(b) IUPAC System

The IUPAC rules for naming alkenes are;

i. Select the longest continuous carbon chain that include the maximum number of double bonds.

ii. The name given to the longest chain will act as parent name, whereby the suffix -ane of the corresponding alkane is replaced by suffix -ene.

iii. If there are two double bonds, the suffix is -diene; for three, -triene; for four, -tetraene; and so on, are used.

iv. Number the chain from the end that gives lower number to the doubly bonded carbons.

v. Since double bond appears between two carbon atoms, therefore its position is indicated by the number of that carbon atom, bearing lower number and this number is written before suffix -ene, -diene etc.

vi. Carbon-carbon double bonds take precedence over alkyl groups in determining the main carbon chain and the direction in which it is numbered.

vii. Name substituent groups as in alkanes, indicating their locations by the number of the main-chain carbon to which they are attached.

viii. For compounds that show geometric isomerism, add the appropriate prefix: cis- or trans-.(see section 16.6)

Tidbit

Now α, β, γ are replaced by numbers 1, 2, 3 in IUPAC.

Examples

16.5.2 Structure

Consider ethene (C₂H₄) to illustrate the structure of alkenes. In ethene, each carbon atom has three sp²-hybridized orbitals which are coplanar. One of the sp²-hybrid orbitals of one carbon atom overlaps linearly with that of another carbon atom to form a sigma (δ) bond. The other two sp²-hybrid orbitals of each carbon atom overlap with 1s orbital of hydrogen atoms to form C-H sigma bonds. The unhybridized p-orbitals of the two carbon atoms, which remain perpendicular to the plane of hybridized orbitals, overlap in a side-wise (parallel) fashion to form a pi (π) bond between the two carbon atoms. (Figure.16.3).

Tidbit

In 1993, the IUPAC recommended a logical change in the positions of the numbers used in names. Instead of placing the numbers before the root name (1-butene), they recommended placing them immediately before the part of the name they locate (but-1-ene).

Figure 16.3 Orbital overlap discription in formation of sigma and pi bonds in ethene.

The overall structure of ethene is planar in which H–C–C and H–C–H bond angles are approximately equal to 120°. The carbon-carbon double bond length is 134 pm and C–H bond lengths are 108 pm.

16.5.3 Conjugation

If an alkene has two double bonds, it is called a diene (or alkadiene), if three double bonds, then triene (or alkatriene) and so on. When two double bonds in an alkene (diene, triene etc) are separated by just one single bond, the two double bonds are said to be conjugated and the alkene is a conjugated alkene. The interaction between the two double bonds in a conjugated dienes (or triene etc.) delocalizes the electron density and increases the stability of the molecule, and termed as conjugation. The simplest diene that can have two conjugated pi bonds is buta-1,3-diene. Similarly hexa-1,3,5-triene is a triene with three conjugated double bonds and so on.
